sections.heading: Place value and order of magnitude

questions.q: Write $4{,}500{,}000$ in the form $a\times10^n$ with $1\leq a<10$.
Find the greatest common divisor (GCD) of $48$ and $60$.
Find the least common multiple (LCM) of $8$ and $12$.
List all the factors of $36$, and state how many there are.
Is $91$ a prime number? Justify your answer.
questions.answer: $91=7\times13$, so it has factors other than $1$ and itself. $91$ is not prime.

questions.q: Find the greatest common factor of $84$ and $126$.
Without dividing, determine whether $4{,}578$ is divisible by $3$.
questions.answer: Digit sum: $4+5+7+8=24$, which is divisible by $3$ (since $24=3\times8$). So $4{,}578$ is divisible by $3$.
Digit sum: $2+3+4+0=9$, which is divisible by $9$. So $2{,}340$ is divisible by $9$.
A number is divisible by $5$ if it ends in $0$ or $5$. Since $715$ ends in $5$, it is divisible by $5$.
Check the last two digits: $44\div4=11$, an integer, so $1{,}244$ is divisible by $4$.

questions.q: Estimate $198\times51$ by rounding each number to the nearest ten, then find the exact product.
questions.answer: Rounded: $200\times50=10{,}000$. Exact: $198\times51=10{,}098$ — close to the estimate.
The third decimal digit is $6$, so round up: $2.49$.

questions.q: Estimate $\sqrt{50}$ to the nearest whole number.
questions.answer: $7^2=49$ and $8^2=64$; since $50$ is closest to $49$, the estimate is $7$ (actual value $\approx7.07$).

questions.q: A shipment weighs approximately $2{,}850$ kg. Round this to the nearest hundred kilograms.
questions.answer: The tens digit is $5$, so round up: $2{,}900$ kg.

questions.q: If $n$ is an even integer, is $n^2+n$ always even, always odd, or can it be either?
questions.answer: Write $n=2k$. Then $n^2+n=4k^2+2k=2(2k^2+k)$, which is always even.

questions.q: Find the remainder when $47$ is divided by $6$.
Is $637$ divisible by $7$? Justify your answer.
List all prime numbers between $30$ and $50$.
questions.answer: Checking each: $31,37,41,43,47$ are prime ($33,35,39,45,49$ are not). That is $5$ primes.

questions.q: If the sum of two integers is odd, is their product always even, always odd, or can it be either?
questions.answer: A sum is odd only when one integer is even and the other is odd. Even $\times$ odd is always even, so the product is always even.

questions.q: A school orders 158 notebooks to be shared as equally as possible among 12 classrooms. How many notebooks does each classroom receive, and how many are left over?
questions.answer: $158\div12=13$ remainder $2$ (since $12\times13=156$). Each classroom receives $13$ notebooks, with $2$ left over.

questions.q: A caterer must seat 250 guests at tables that each hold 8 people. What is the minimum number of tables required?
questions.answer: $250\div8=31.25$. Since a partial table still needs a full table, round up: $32$ tables.

questions.q: Three friends share a restaurant bill of 186 riyals equally, then each adds a 10-riyal tip. How much does each person pay in total?
questions.answer: Each share of the bill: $186\div3=62$ riyals. Adding the tip: $62+10=72$ riyals per person.

questions.q: A red light flashes every 8 seconds and a green light flashes every 12 seconds. If both flash together right now, after how many seconds will they next flash together at the same time?
questions.answer: The lights next align after the LCM of $8$ and $12$, which is $24$ seconds.
